title: Design token bridge & thermostat controls for cost heatmap and rollout-state patterns
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Background: Cost and rollout views in the Console surface dense quantitative signals (token spend, P50/P95 latency, cache hit rate) alongside qualitative rollout states (canary, ramp, fallback). Current components reuse color tokens intended for alerts and status pills which overloads semantics and creates noisy dashboards. Goal: define a design token bridge and compact interaction control ("thermostat") for continuous cost heatmaps and discrete rollout states that is accessible, composable, and easy for engineers to map to runtime metrics and rollout policies.

Proposed Deliverables:
- Token spec: gradient ramps (4 stops) for cost intensity, paired with neutral baseline tokens and a set of anchored tokens for rollout states (canary, stable, degraded, fallback). Tokens expressed as Figma variables and tokens.json naming convention.
- Thermostat control component: single-axis slider with discrete ticks for rollout stages and an overlay heatmap preview for cost sensitivity.
- Compact legend & mini-sparkline component to show per-route cost trend with token-driven color.
- Accessibility pass: WCAG 2.1 contrast for all token pairs, keyboard affordances for thermostat, ARIA labels for heatmap cells.
- Implementation handoff: annotated Figma file, tokens export, example React component props and mapping guidelines for ENG (continuousValue -> gradient token, state -> anchor token).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Figma tokens exported and conform to naming pattern console.tokens.cost.* and console.tokens.rollout.*
- Thermostat component prototype (click/drag + discrete snap) tested in Figma and validated with PMs on three common routes (search, embeddings, chat).
- Color ramps meet 4.5:1 contrast for text overlays at normal sizes or provide accessible alternate overlay.
- Engineering can map two example metrics (daily spend per route, 7d trend) to tokens using the provided mapping doc.

Constraints & Trade-offs:
- We keep existing alert/pill tokens intact to avoid a large migration. New cost ramps will be additive and scoped to dashboard/insights surfaces.
- Gradient ramps optimized for perceptual uniformity; will use lab color tuning instead of naive hex interpolation. Slightly increases token count but reduces ambiguity.

Notes on developer ergonomics:
- Prefer token names that are numeric-ordinal (cost.100, cost.300, cost.500, cost.900) to reflect intensity and to be friendly to programmatic thresholds.
- Provide JSON and CSS variables for quick rollout and a recommended map for common thresholds (low < $0.05/token, medium $0.05–0.20, high > $0.20).

Deliverable timeline: prototyping + internal review (this ticket), then two-week dev spike (ENG-20421) for token export and small UI component implementation in Storybook.

Sign-offs required: Lead PM (Maya Singh), Design Lead (Kara O'Neill), Eng owner (Ravi Patel).
comments: 2025-02-11 — Ava Martinez: Initial exploration uploaded to Figma (iter A/B/C). Iter A uses a warm-cool ramp; Iter B uses monochrome ramp with saturation modulation. Early feedback from Kara: prefer warm-coded intensity for cost (natural association).

2025-02-14 — Kara O'Neill: Design review notes: 1) ensure tokens support text overlays for small numbers; 2) thermostat needs discrete 'pause' tick for manual hold during rollouts; 3) legend must be usable at 240px width. Added 'accessibility' label for contrast pass.

2025-02-18 — Liam Chen: Built interactive Figma prototype for thermostat with snap-to-tick interactions; uploaded example props for React component. Raised dependency ENG-19872 for metrics mapping API.

2025-02-22 — Maya Singh (PM): Validated with product analytics — the three routes chosen have distinct distribution shapes; mapping guidance looks good. Requested a low-fidelity microcopy pass for the thermostat (tooltip language when hovering ticks).

2025-02-25 — Accessibility review (external consultant): Color ramps A and C pass contrast for 14px text but fail for 12px. Recommendation: provide 'high-contrast' alternate tokens and reduce reliance on text overlays on smallest heatmap cells. Added action item to provide alt pattern (hatching) for colorblind users.

2025-03-01 — Eng review (Ravi Patel): Reviewed mapping guidelines and proposed telemetry fields. Noted potential perf issue when rendering heatmaps with live streaming metrics on low-end clients; recommends server-side pre-binning and caching. Added dependency ENG-20421 to implement a small API for pre-binned heatmap payloads.

2025-03-04 — Design review (Kara O'Neill): Addressed comments: added high-contrast tokens, implemented hatching overlay option in prototype, refined token names to console.tokens.cost.100/300/500/900. Ready for final handoff.

2025-03-05 — Liam Chen: Prepared handoff bundle and opened implementation PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/6842 with Storybook stories and token JSON. Marking ticket as In Review awaiting PM + Accessibility sign-off.
next_steps: PM sign-off on microcopy and rollout language
Accessibility team final sign-off on high-contrast tokens
Engineer spike (ENG-20421) to implement pre-binned heatmap API and test performance
Merge PR and publish tokens to design system registry
Create a short rollout plan for migrating dashboard instances to new tokens (opt-in flag for 2 releases)
